description: MB-3 HEADLINE golden (docs/design/multi-body.md §MB-3 / §Decisions-4): a downstream fillet on an edge CREATED by a boolean. Six features: (1) a 20x20 mm square on the XY origin datum at x,y in [0,20]; (2) extrude add 20 mm up -> body A, a 20x20x20 cube; (3) a second 20x20 mm square at x in [10,30] (overlapping A in x[10,20], same y,z); (4) extrude add 20 mm up merge=FALSE -> body B, a second 20x20x20 cube; (5) a `boolean` union (target=A / tool=B) -> the fused 30x20x20 box (A and B tile x[0,30] with full y,z; clean() merges the seams to a canonical 12-edge box, so the four VERTICAL corner edges at x=0 and x=30 are BOOLEAN-CREATED edges of the fused result); (6) a `fillet` of radius 2 mm on ONE picked vertical corner edge of the fused box (the edge at x=0, y=0, z in [0,20]), named by a stage-1 EdgeSignature picked-edge SubshapeRef anchored to the boolean feature. THE PROOF (design §MB-3): the fillet resolves the boolean-created edge to EXACTLY ONE edge on a clean rebuild -- the fused body's edges get stage-1 signatures like any primitive's -- so 'you can round an edge of a combined part' works end to end, byte-identical GLB+STEP across an interpreter restart. The honest degrade-under-topology-changing-edit limit is covered in test_boolean.py (not a golden -- a degraded rebuild has no body to measure) and documented in the BooleanParamsV1 v1-limits docstring + design §MB-3.
derivation: Expectations are HAND-DERIVED analytic values, not recorded harness output (geometry-gates skill: a golden recorded from buggy output enshrines the bug). The fused body is a 30x20x20 rectangular box spanning x[0,30], y[0,20], z[0,20] (union of A[0,20]^3 and B[10,30]x[0,20]x[0,20]; see boolean-union-two-cubes-overlap for that derivation). The fillet rounds ONE vertical edge -- the x=0,y=0 corner, running z[0,20] -- with radius r=2 mm over the full height h=20 mm. A fillet on a convex box edge replaces the sharp 90-degree corner with a quarter-cylinder of radius r tangent to the two adjacent faces at distance r from the edge.

volume: the material removed is the corner region between the square corner (r x r cross-section) and the quarter disk (radius r): cross-section area removed = r^2 - pi*r^2/4, over height h. removed = h*(r^2 - pi*r^2/4) = 20*(4 - pi) = 80 - 20*pi. volume = 30*20*20 - (80 - 20*pi) = 12000 - 80 + 20*pi = 11920 + 20*pi = 11982.831853071795 mm^3. Measured deviation: 0.0.

surface_area: start from the box's 3200 mm^2. The two side faces adjacent to the filleted edge each lose a strip r x h: -2*(r*h) = -2*(2*20) = -80. The top and bottom faces each lose the square-minus-quarter-disk corner: -2*(r^2 - pi*r^2/4) = -2*(4 - pi) = -8 + 2*pi. The quarter-cylinder fillet face adds arc-length (2*pi*r/4) times height h = (pi*r/2)*h = (pi*2/2)*20 = 20*pi. Total = 3200 - 80 + (-8 + 2*pi) + 20*pi = 3112 + 22*pi = 3181.1150383789754 mm^2. Measured deviation: 0.0.

centroid: box centroid (15,10,10) at V=12000; the removed corner sliver has volume Vr = 80 - 20*pi and, in cross-section, first moment about x = r^2*(r/2) - (pi*r^2/4)*(r - 4r/(3*pi)) = 20/3 - 2*pi (for r=2), so its x first moment over the body is h*(20/3 - 2*pi) = 400/3 - 40*pi (and the same about y by the x=y symmetry of the corner; z is mid-height 10 exactly). centroid_x = (12000*15 - (400/3 - 40*pi)) / (11920 + 20*pi) = (180000 - 400/3 + 40*pi)/(11920 + 20*pi) = 15.020850878973928; centroid_y = (120000 - 400/3 + 40*pi)/(11920 + 20*pi) = 10.013687235546936; centroid_z = 10.0 exactly. The fillet removes material from the x=0,y=0 corner, so the centroid shifts slightly +x and +y. Measured deviation: 0.0 on all three.

bounding_box = [0,0,0]..[30,20,20]: the fillet is tangent to the x=0 and y=0 faces, so it does not change the outer envelope (the box's own extent). All six bounds are analytically exact; measured deviation is ~4.4e-16 on min.x and min.y (the fillet tangent point sampled at machine-epsilon off 0), 0.0 elsewhere.

topology = 7 faces, 15 edges, 1 SHELL. faces: the 6 box faces + 1 new cylindrical fillet face = 7. edges: the 1 filleted vertical edge is removed and replaced by the fillet face's boundary -- 2 vertical tangent lines (where the fillet meets the two side faces) + 2 quarter-arc edges (where it meets the top and bottom faces): 12 - 1 + 4 = 15. shells = 1 (still one connected solid -- the fillet is a local modification of the single post-boolean body). Euler-Poincare cross-check: the solid stays a valid closed genus-0 manifold (V - E + F = 2 with V = 10 vertices: the original 8 minus the 2 filleted-corner vertices plus 4 new tangent/arc vertices -> 10 - 15 + 7 = 2).

mesh = 154 vertices / 140 triangles at the golden's linear 0.1 mm / angular 0.1 rad deflection: the 6 planar faces tessellate as before but the CYLINDRICAL fillet face is faceted into a fan of quads across the quarter-arc (the deflection sets the facet count), so the count is higher than a pure box's 24/12. Asserted EXACTLY (a changed count is a real tessellation change) and byte-deterministic across rebuilds/restarts within one kernel version; the absolute value is the deterministic OCCT tessellation at this deflection, cross-checked by the byte-identical GLB gate (not independently hand-countable for the curved face, unlike a planar-only golden).

GLB byte size is deliberately NOT pinned: it is asserted deterministic (byte-identical) by the runner within one kernel version, but pinning the absolute size would break on every glTF-writer upgrade without geometric meaning.
tolerance_rationale: Measured first, then set (geometry-gates skill: never copy a bound blindly). The filleted fused box's volume (11920 + 20*pi), surface_area (3112 + 22*pi), and centroid are analytic closed forms; measured deviations vs those closed forms (2026-07-18, build123d 0.11.1 / OCCT 7.9, planegcs 0.8.0) are EXACTLY 0.0 for volume, surface_area, and all three centroid components, and 0.0 for four bounding-box bounds with ~4.4e-16 mm on min.x / min.y (the fillet tangent point sampled at machine epsilon off zero). Documented ceiling 1e-9 (matching the sibling boolean / multibody goldens) is ~2e6x the observed worst case (~4.4e-16, a bbox bound), headroom for platform FP variation across OCCT builds and the STEP round-trip re-measure, while staying 5 orders of magnitude tighter than the standing kernel linear tolerance (1e-7 m -> 1e-4 mm at model scale). The fillet is an exact OCCT BRepFilletAPI operation on an analytically-round edge; the solver contributes zero error by construction (shape-pinned squares; solved == input). Loosening this further requires a reviewed kernel-level justification recorded here and in docs/GEOMETRY-QA.md.
